what_its_for: Somapacitan-beco is a long-acting growth hormone used to treat adults whose bodies do not make enough growth hormone on their own. This condition is called adult growth hormone deficiency. It helps improve body composition, energy levels, and overall well-being.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection) once a week. You will inject it into fatty areas of your body such as your stomach (abdomen), thighs, or upper arms. Rotate your injection sites each week — do not inject into the same spot twice in a row. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to prepare and give yourself the injection. Always follow their instructions carefully. Use the pre-filled pen device exactly as shown. Never shake the pen. Do not inject into skin that is red, sore, bruised, or hard.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your blood tests and how you respond to treatment. The usual starting dose is 1.5 mg injected under the skin once a week. Your doctor may slowly increase or adjust your dose over time, usually every 2 to 4 weeks, to find the best dose for you. The maximum dose is generally 8 mg per week. Women who take estrogen pills by mouth may need a higher dose than women who use estrogen patches or gels.
missed_dose: If you miss your weekly dose, take it as soon as you remember — as long as it is within 3 days of your scheduled injection day. After giving the missed dose, continue your regular weekly schedule. If it has been more than 3 days since your missed dose, skip it and give your next dose on your usual scheduled day. Do not take two doses in one week to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store your unused Sogroya pens in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze the pen — if it freezes, throw it away and use a new one. After you first use a pen, you may keep it in the refrigerator or at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 6 weeks. Write down the date you first used the pen. Throw it away after 6 weeks even if medicine is still left inside. Keep all pens away from children. Do not use the pen if the medicine looks cloudy, discolored, or has particles in it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid injecting into the same spot week after week to prevent skin changes such as lumps or dents under the skin. Do not shake the pen, as this can damage the medicine. Avoid exposing the pen to extreme heat or direct sunlight. Talk to your doctor before starting any new medications, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, as growth hormone can interact with medicines for diabetes, thyroid conditions, seizures, and steroids. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as this medicine should not be used during pregnancy.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: sudden or severe headache, changes in your vision, nausea or vomiting (which could be signs of increased pressure in the brain); hip or knee pain, or a limp (which could be a sign of a hip joint problem); severe stomach pain that spreads to your back (possible sign of pancreatitis); signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst, frequent urination, or blurry vision; unusual changes in a mole or skin lesion; swelling in your hands, feet, or ankles; muscle or joint pain that is new or worsening; or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also tell your doctor if you feel your medicine is not working or if you have any new health problems.
when_it_works: You may not notice changes right away. It can take several weeks to months before you start to feel the full benefits, such as improved energy, better body composition (less body fat, more muscle), and an improved sense of well-being. Your doctor will monitor your progress with blood tests and check-ups to make sure the medicine is working properly and your dose is right for you.
special_populations: Older adults (age 60 and above) may be more sensitive to the effects of growth hormone and are often started on lower doses to reduce the risk of side effects. Women who take estrogen by mouth (oral estrogen) may need a higher dose because oral estrogen can reduce the effect of growth hormone — talk to your doctor about the best approach for you. This medicine is NOT approved for use in children. It should not be used if you have active cancer, certain eye problems related to diabetes (diabetic retinopathy), critical illness due to surgery or serious medical events, or if you are pregnant. Always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions before starting this medicine.
